criteria.description: If this region is wrong, a number the papers cite is wrong and nothing downstream notices. Weighted by how far a silent error would travel before anything caught it.

This region is what makes a result attributable to the code that produced it: fingerprints, tolerances, generated indices. Its failure mode is a figure that still verifies while describing a previous build.
This region exists to refuse. It encodes a measured breakpoint the rig has already been burned by, and its job is to fail loudly rather than return a plausible number from outside the window.
What this software is, per its maintainers: a known-answer calibration rig whose whole value is that its answers are checkable. Authored as a single ordering, not computed by PREP.

members.rationale: Two anchors on one claim: the member is the byte-identity, so either file drifting alone is the event worth catching. Everything else in the manifest reads through this file.

aspects.claim: hodge.py and design/reference/hodge.py are byte-identical, and git's own SHA-256 is the proof rather than a convention.
Every operator, projector and decomposition the rig uses comes from this file; the rig is a data source and never reimplements the decomposition.
analyze_flow and analyze_comparisons are different tests with different default fillings, so the rig always passes filling explicitly and logs it.

members.rationale: The highest trap-density region in the repo: three measured breakpoints and the exception that fires on them. Split into two anchors so the thresholds and the gate that reads them fail independently.

aspects.claim: regime_report with strict=True raises RegimeViolation naming the failed gates; a loud failure is the intended output, because outside the window floor + c/k fits anyway and silently misreports the floor.
Both bounds are closed-form — saturation is a mean over p**k_min + (1-p)**k_min and mildness is eps squared over gradient energy — so the window is checked before anything is sampled or fitted.
The c-oracle gate is labelled necessary but not sufficient in both code and spec: it passes at beta = 0.25 while the recovered floor is 1.86 times wrong.
The three constants are annotated as measured breakpoints rather than preferences, with 0.17 fitting and 0.42 breaking recorded at the saturation bound.

members.rationale: One of the three findings the build had to fix, and the one whose docstring already records its own staleness incident. High correctness load because the wrong window returns a floor rather than an error.

aspects.claim: The window is c_oracle / (rho * floor_target), not the spec's fixed 64, because it is set by the ratio of the variance term to the floor and not by a constant.
On filling='empty' the calibration graph has b1 = 20 and c around 160, so k = 64 leaves the variance term about ten times too large and recovers 0.016 against a true 0.090.
rho is required with no default because it is a shipped config field, and the docstring records the v6-to-v7 incident where a default here went stale unnoticed.
A floor_target of zero returns infinity rather than dividing, because the eps = 0 negative control is judged by whether its CI covers zero and not by this window.

members.rationale: The estimator itself. Anchored from line 1 so the module docstring, which carries the measured bias figures, cannot drift away from the code it describes.

aspects.claim: The fit is restricted to k >= fit_k_min before the design matrix is built, because a two-parameter OLS absorbs the O(1/k^2) logit-bias term into the intercept — 0.83x-2.48x bias on the full grid against 0.87x-0.95x on k >= 64.
Fewer than two points inside the window raises ValueError, and the message says to extend the k grid upward rather than lower fit_k_min.
The result carries n_fit_points, fit_k_min and the actual k_fitted list, so a floor is never readable without the window that produced it.
The floor ships with a bootstrap interval across seeds and a separates_from_zero flag, because its job is to be distinguished from zero.

members.rationale: Pure trap. Without it a destroyed flow reports a clean zero harmonic reading, which is the most convincing wrong answer the rig can produce.

aspects.claim: An edge inside the representable band |Y| <= log((k+1)/(k-1)) is ordinary quantization loss reported through the residual; the entire flow quantizing to zero is a different event and raises.
The guard fires only when the target has energy and the achieved flow has none, so it does not fire on partial loss.
EmissionCollapse reports the location, k, the dead-edge count and the band width, then names the two remedies: the sign path for a plus-minus-one rule, or a larger emit_k.

members.rationale: The mechanism the whole provenance criterion rests on. Its own test suite already pins the sensitive/blind distinction; the member records what that distinction is for.

aspects.claim: The hash is taken over a docstring-stripped normalized AST dump, so it is stable across comments, blank lines and reindentation and changes when any body or constant in the closure changes.

It walks module-level names from the entry point by repeated reference resolution until a round adds nothing, bounded by _max_depth, so the fingerprint covers everything the entry actually depends on.
Sibling module aliases are added to the known set so references through them count, but routed to reached rather than the frontier and folded in via _sibling_parts.
A module with no module-level definition by that name returns None rather than hashing an empty closure into a plausible-looking value.

members.rationale: The registry's actual comparison. Every cited number in both papers passes through this function, and its failure mode is the quiet one: a green run against a claim set that has moved.

aspects.claim: A failure prints the claim, the stored value, the fresh value and the drift, so a reader can see whether the conclusion moved or only the digits did.
Paths present on only one side are collected as a set and returned with infinite drift, rather than allowing a tolerance verdict on the surviving overlap of a restructured claim.
check_provenance compares the claim ids parsed out of PROVENANCE.md against the registry keys in both directions, because the index is generated and nothing else keeps it current.

members.rationale: Added after four cited_in references were wrong at once and two of them shipped to main. The region is a checker with nothing behind it: if the counter model drifts from TeX, the checks built on it go green against a wrong baseline. Scored high on provenance because cited_in's whole job is attribution, and its failure mode is the one that criterion names -- a citation that still verifies while describing a previous revision.

aspects.claim: Numbering is recomputed from the .tex sources in document order, never read from a built PDF, which is what lets the check run with no LaTeX toolchain and is also why nothing compares the model against TeX's own output.

It is exact only because every \newtheorem in both papers is declared without a [section] reset (six in bridge-invariance, two in calibration-methodology) and neither paper uses a starred heading; the anchors cover those preamble blocks so either side moving alone is caught.

Checking that Proposition 3 exists passes a reference that names the wrong proposition, which is how gradient-annihilated and b1-non-monotone were wrong by one and shipped to main; the title is matched against the environment at that number.

Every reference naming a numbered environment must carry that environment's title, as a per-entry rule rather than a floor on how many do, because a count neither prevents decay nor binds the next entry added -- the case that produced the defects. sec, fig, table and file references are exempt.
